panel_chico.dato: At 5.2 AU, only 3.7% of the sunlight we receive on Earth reaches the spacecraft.

panel_mediano.dato: Enough for Mars, insufficient for Jupiter.

panel_gigante.dato: Juno was the first spacecraft to reach Jupiter powered by solar energy, using 3 massive wings.

rtg.dato: They do not rely on the Sun and their waste heat warms the spacecraft, but plutonium-238 is expensive and scarce.

antena_media.dato: The signal weakens with the square of the distance.

antena_alta.dato: Larger diameter = more focused beam = more data.

antena_ka.dato: Ka-band enables measuring Jupiter's gravity using the Doppler effect.

blindaje_ninguno.dato: Jupiter has the most intense radiation belts in the solar system.

blindaje_aluminio.dato: Lightweight and inexpensive, but only stops half of the radiation.

boveda_titanio.dato: Juno protects its electronics inside a titanium radiation vault.

tanque_chico.dato: Every kilogram of propellant must also be launched.

tanque_mediano.dato: Just enough margin to arrive and brake.

tanque_grande.dato: More than half of Juno's liftoff mass was propellant.

mwr.dato: Peers hundreds of kilometers beneath the clouds to measure water and ammonia.

gravedad.dato: Measuring how Jupiter pulls on the spacecraft reveals whether it has a solid core.

mag.dato: The magnetic field reveals the "dynamo" inside the planet.

jiram.dato: Sees the heat escaping from deep layers and the auroras.

particulas.dato: Measure the particles that create the most powerful auroras in the solar system.

uvs_waves.dato: Listens to radio waves and photographs auroras in ultraviolet.

junocam.dato: Its photos are processed by the public: citizen science.

camara_hd.dato: Spectacular photos... if you manage to downlink them.

sonda_atmosferica.dato: The Galileo mission dropped a probe in 1995; it survived less than an hour.

lroc.dato: Its photos are so detailed that tracks and landing modules from the Apollo missions are visible.

lend.dato: Neutrons bouncing off the surface reveal hydrogen: a clue for water ice.

lola.dato: Fires laser pulses and measures how long they take to return, building an elevation map.

diviner.dato: Measures ground temperature: permanently shadowed polar craters are cold enough for ice to survive billions of years.

lamp.dato: Sees in the dark using the faint ultraviolet glow of starlight.

crater.dato: Measures how much radiation an astronaut would receive: key for returning to the Moon.

minirf.dato: Radar penetrates shadow and dust to search for ice inside craters.

bateria_basica.dato: Batteries store the solar panels' energy to ride through eclipses, when the Sun is blocked and nothing is generated.

bateria_avanzada.dato: More cells in the same space last through longer eclipses, but they take longer to test and qualify.

computadora_estandar.dato: The spacecraft's brain: it runs commands and holds data until the antenna can send it.

computadora_rad_hard.dato: "Rad-hard" chips survive radiation and their large memory holds data when the link falls short. They cost more and take longer to qualify.

orientacion_basica.dato: Reaction wheels spin to point the spacecraft without using fuel; sun sensors tell it where it is facing.

orientacion_precision.dato: A star tracker recognizes the sky like a map and points with great precision, which improves photos and the link.
